quick_brief: Week 5 Challenge: Test your advanced skills in programming random decision-making rules and designing the architecture of huge multi-screen applications such as a smart doctor’s clinic!

questions.text: Which block of code is used to select a completely random item from a list of choices (rock, paper, scissors) to simulate phone intelligence?
When building large applications consisting of multiple screens (such as a doctor's office application), how do we send the registered patient name to the advanced booking screen?
options: Use open another screen with start value
questions.correct: Use open another screen with start value

questions.text: Which brick do we use inside the second screen to receive and read the value sent to it (the patient’s name, for example) from the first screen?
In the game rock-paper-scissors, to compare the equivalence of choices, we check the logical condition:
options: if get userChoice and get pcChoice

questions.text: The integrated medical clinic application consists of several screens. Which screen is used to calculate prices for medical services and book an examination appointment?
Which property in the CheckBox element is used to programmatically check whether the user has selected a specific medical option such as a dental check-up service?
If we open another screen with start value (screenName = "Home", startValue = "Hello"). What value will get start value return in the Home screen?
To update the patient's bill and increase it by $50 when selecting a medical service, we write the equation:
options: set global total to (get global total + 50)
set global total to (50 - get global total)
questions.correct: set global total to (get global total + 50)

questions.text: Which HTML element do we use to display the doctor's office options (teeth, eyes, children) in a drop-down list from which the user can choose one option?
When building a medical application, to get a random number of doctor's reservation code for a patient, we use a building block:
Write code to select a random item from a list containing items ('rock', 'paper', 'scissors') and assign the value to a variable named global_pc.
questions.correct_code: set global_pc to call pick a random item (list = create empty list ["stone", "paper", "scissors"])

questions.text: Type the code to go to a screen called 'ClinicScreen', sending the text value 'Eye Clinic' as the starting value for the patient.
questions.correct_code: call open another screen with start value (screenName = "ClinicScreen", startValue = "Eye Clinic")
